scale.1: meets only with high risk or effort

decisions.D1: First P1 step at 10 minutes by default, configurable
decisions.D2: Only Owners and Admins edit rules
decisions.D3: A suggested priority never starts an escalation
decisions.D4: Business hours belong to the rule
decisions.D5: No SMS in version 1; a webhook event instead
decisions.D6: Targets are named users; no rotas in version 1
decisions.D7: Flood cap of 20 escalation emails per target per hour
decisions.D8: Numeric targets that no source states
decisions.D9: Acknowledgement ends escalation, and fired steps do not repeat

drivers.title: Confidence that means something
drivers.note: Not architecture-significant: met by the triage evaluation (Chapter 7), whatever the structure.

drivers.title: Rule permissions enforced on the server; every change audited for 400 days
At most 20 escalation emails per target per hour, across all rules
Targets are workspace user IDs only
Owner and Admins emailed within 5 minutes of a P1 rule change
No task title, description or comments in emails or webhook events
Rule editor meets WCAG 2.2 AA; keyboard only
drivers.note: Not architecture-significant: a property of the editor's interface, the same in every option.

drivers.title: 95% of steps within 60 seconds; a stalled evaluator pages after 5 minutes
$0 per notification beyond email and webhooks; no paid messaging service
Operable by Relay's eight engineers on one platform on-call rota
drivers.source: Chapter 1 (team of eight engineers); Lab 2.2 docs (on-call)

drivers.title: Ships on the daily deploy train, every weekday at 15:00 UTC
API limit of 600 requests per minute per token, HTTP 429 with Retry-After
No API request waits for the triage model; API p95 under 1 second
drivers.source: sam.o, recorded in ADR-007; the model's p95 is 4.12 s in Chapter 2's evaluation

drivers.title: Webhook deliveries signed, retried 8 times over about 6 hours, safe to receive twice
Triage capacity can grow without growing the rest of Relay
